title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues an axiomatic set-up built on the previous pages. There are four pieces of data. A is a set of 'figures'. ⊴ is an order relation on A (probably a sub-figure or incidence order). |·| is a 'support' map that sends a figure to the 'space it occupies'. ≪ is a primitive relation between figures; the dotted variant ≪° (≪ with a small circle) is a refinement of it, apparently defined through the maximal chains X°. To each figure X the notes attach its set of 'déploiements' (unfoldings) Dép(X). These are subsets of an ordered set Σ that has a complement ∁. The next page states the requirements on such a family 𝔖: (a) each member is non-empty; (b) any two distinct members are disjoint, written S ≤ ∁T or T ≤ ∁S.

The previous page proved a necessary condition R for X ≪ Y. For every S in Dép X there is a T in Dép Y with S ≤ T; this T is necessarily unique and is written φ(S). The resulting map φ: Dép X → Dép Y is increasing. In other words, the unfoldings of X refine into the unfoldings of Y. A 'classification' is defined to be 'spatial' when R is also sufficient.

This page first comments on the name. 'Spatial' means that the primitive relation ≪ can be recovered from ⊴ and |·| alone, that is, from purely spatial notions. The support plays the role of the 'space occupied by a figure'. This sets up a recognition (representation) problem: given a bare structure (A, ⊴, |·|), when does it come from a spatial classification structure (A, ⊴, ≪°, |·|)?

The proposed strategy runs as follows. From (A, ⊴, |·|) one builds an ordered set Σ. Σ carries an extra structure 𝒞 that lets one define the support |·| on Σ itself. One also builds two maps:
- X ↦ Dép(X);
- A → Figel^ord(Σ), the set of 'ordered elementary figures' of Σ, i.e. the families satisfying (a) and (b).
The margin note (marked *) says that, besides axiom At 4, conditions (i) and (ii) must be checked.

The next page carries the strategy further. Comparing déploiements, Dép X ≪ Dép Y, gives a preorder on A. Condition (ii), that Dép X = Dép Y implies X = Y, makes it an order. The goal is then to show that ≪ on A is induced from the corresponding relation on Figel(Σ). In effect this is a representation theorem: realise an abstract 'figure calculus' inside a concrete calculus of families of disjoint regions of a space-like ordered set.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page; it is set-up and motivation only. The construction of Σ and 𝒞 is announced but not given here.

On the next page, condition (b) reads 'S ≤ ∁T or T ≤ ∁S'. In a Boolean algebra (or with any symmetric pseudo-complement) these two alternatives are equivalent, so the disjunction is redundant. Either ∁ is meant to be a non-symmetric operation or the 'or' is just a slip.

The previous page left a gap: the claim that φ is 'necessarily unique' is justified there by the argument T∩T' = ∅ ⇒ S = ∅. That argument uses condition (b) on Dép(Y) together with non-emptiness of S.

ideas.what: Definition of a 'spatial' classification: the primitive relation X ≪ Y holds exactly when every déploiement of X lies in a unique déploiement of Y (an increasing refinement map Dép X → Dép Y)
ideas.modern_name: Representation of an abstract part/region relation by refinement of families of disjoint regions; akin to mereotopological representation theorems and Stone-type duality for posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereotopology representation results (e.g. Düntsch–Winter, Stell, Roeper for region-based contact algebras, 1990s–2000s); Stone duality (1936)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA/Esquisse/Pursuing Stacks as far as I know; possibly related to unpublished 'tame topology' musings

ideas.what: Recognition problem: when does a structure (A, ⊴, |·|) come from a spatial classification, via construction of an ordered set Σ with support structure 𝒞 and an embedding A → Figel^ord(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Representation / realization theorem (concrete model of an axiomatic incidence-support structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General model-theoretic or representation-theoretic practice; no specific attribution

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatics of 'figures' with support and 'déploiements' and poses a representation theorem: recover the primitive relation ≪ purely spatially from ⊴ and |·|. The proof strategy is only begun on this page and the next.
missed.quote: Cela nous mène devant la question : étant donnée une structure (A, ⊴, |·|), sous quelles conditions provient-elle d'une structure de classification spatiale (A, ⊴, ≪°, |·|) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with representation theorems in region-based (mereo)topology and with combinatorial models of stratified or tame spaces. However, the context is too fragmentary to claim a missed result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an idiosyncratic, unpublished axiomatic set-up (support, déploiements, spatial classification) that is interesting as a record of Grothendieck's 1986 'Ateliers' thinking. The page itself contains only definitions-in-progress and a posed question, with no result.
transcription_corrections: 'en aussi suffisante' should be 'est aussi suffisante'.
'd'une structure de schéma[?] spatial' should most likely read 'd'une structure de classification spatiale', consistent with the definition on the previous page.
'X ⟶ Sup(X)' should be 'X ⟶ Dép(X)'; the image clearly shows Dép.
The margin note likely reads '* + l'axiome At 4 [?] ... il y a à vérifier les conditions (i) et (ii)'. 'AS 4' should be 'At 4', matching 'At 1 a) b) c)' on the next page.
The added line should read '(si Figel ord(Σ) désigne l'ens. des figures élém. ord. de Σ qui ...)'. In the image 'ord' is written as a superscript on Figel and 'élém.' is inserted above the line.
